report_name: Thermo Fisher DNA Software Flaw Allows Undetectable Evidence Tampering

attack_patterns.name: Stored Data Manipulation
attack_patterns.description: The vulnerability in Thermo Fisher's software allows a malicious actor to alter digital DNA files (.fsa and .hid) without detection, compromising the integrity of the stored data.

attack_patterns.name: Craft Adversarial Data
attack_patterns.description: A researcher demonstrated the vulnerability by using an AI tool to merge two distinct DNA profiles into a single, seemingly valid file that the software opened without any warnings or errors.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-17583
vulnerabilities.description: A high-severity vulnerability in Thermo Fisher Scientific's Applied Biosystems software that fails to perform cryptographic integrity checks on DNA analysis files (.fsa, .hid), allowing for undetectable modification of forensic evidence.

identities.name: Thermo Fisher Scientific
identities.description: The vendor of the affected Applied Biosystems human identification (HID) software suite who released patches for the vulnerability.

identities.name: Forensic Laboratories
identities.description: A class of affected organizations, including crime labs at local, state, and federal levels that use the vulnerable software to analyze evidence from crime scenes.

identities.name: Clinical Laboratories
identities.description: A class of affected organizations, including hospitals and diagnostic centers that use the vulnerable software for genetic testing and disease diagnosis.

identities.name: Research Institutions
identities.description: A class of affected organizations, including universities and biotech companies that use the vulnerable software for genetic research.

indicators.name: Suspicious Modification of Forensic DNA Files
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Modification of Forensic DNA Files (.fsa, .hid)
id: 4b9c1d8e-3a2b-4f6c-8d7e-9a0b1c2d3e4f
status: experimental
description: Detects file write or modification events involving Thermo Fisher DNA analysis files (.fsa, .hid). This could indicate evidence tampering, potentially exploiting CVE-2026-17583.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/thermo-fisher-patches-flaw-that-could.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-04
tags:
  - attack.t1565.001
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.fsa'
      - '.hid'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects file write or modification events involving Thermo Fisher DNA analysis files (.fsa, .hid), as suggested in the report's hunting hints. This could indicate evidence tampering related to CVE-2026-17583.

indicators.name: Binary Editor Accessing Forensic DNA Files
indicators.pattern:
title: Binary Editor Accessing Forensic DNA Files
id: f8a7b6c5-4d3e-4c2b-8a19-0f9e8d7c6b5a
status: experimental
description: Detects known binary or hex editors accessing Thermo Fisher DNA analysis files (.fsa, .hid). This could indicate an attempt to tamper with forensic evidence, potentially exploiting CVE-2026-17583.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/thermo-fisher-patches-flaw-that-could.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-04
tags:
  - attack.t1565.001
  - attack.impact
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_editors:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\HxD.exe'
      - '\hexeditor.exe'
      - '\frhed.exe'
      - '\wxHexEditor.exe'
      - '\cygnus.exe'
      - '\FlexHex.exe'
  selection_files:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.fsa'
      - '.hid'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects the use of hex editors or binary modification tools on forensic evidence files, as suggested in the report's hunting hints for detecting potential evidence tampering.
